findings.source_quote: It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.
findings.suggested_fix: Adjust wording to better reflect the original English list and avoid possible semantic shifts or unintended duplication. For example, translate each English item distinctly and in reasonable Indonesian equivalents: "Kekecewaan, Keraguan, Kesedihan, Kehancuran, Kekecewaan yang nyata (disillusionment), Keputusasaan, Suram, Kekalahan, Putus asa, Depresi, Putus asa (despair), Penghancuran, Penipuan, dan Kematian." (Keep consistent single-word translations and avoid repeating synonyms for the same English term.)
findings.translation_quote: Tampak cukup kebetulan bahwa begitu banyak kata-kata dengan konotasi negatif diawali dengan huruf D: Kekecewaan, Keraguan, Duka, Kehancuran, Kepahitan, Kegelapan, Kekalahan, Keputusasaan, Depresi, Musnah, Penghancuran, Penipuan, dan Kematian.

findings.source_quote: The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the measurement term to a conventional Indonesian historical unit or explicitly keep the approximation. Suggestion: translate as "sekitar enam puluh furlong (kira-kira tujuh mil)" or "sekitar enam puluh furlong (kira-kira tujuh mil/11 kilometer)". This preserves the original term "furlong" while providing the familiar metric approximation for readers.
findings.translation_quote: Jalan dari Yerusalem ke Emmaus adalah sekitar enam puluh stadion atau kira-kira tujuh mil.
